target.title: feat: clarify iOS Location Always permission flow
target.body:
Related: #99229
Related: #86217
Related closed candidate: #99235

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where iOS users could select Location Always in OpenClaw without the app clearly explaining whether iOS had actually granted background-capable location access. That made wake-up/location workflows ambiguous when iOS only allowed While Using, denied access, global Location Services were disabled, or the user changed OpenClaw/iOS location settings independently.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an explicit iOS permission summary for Location settings that separates the user's selected OpenClaw mode from the effective iOS authorization state. It also wires the background-location contract into the native configuration and location service path: background updates are only enabled for Always-capable use, significant-change monitoring is stopped when the mode is disabled, downgraded, or no longer authorized Always, and app-level Location Off remains a sticky OpenClaw preference even when iOS still grants permission.

This follows the current SettingsProTab pattern for now because #99231 may reshape the Settings UI.

#99235 explored a similar area but was closed after it expanded beyond the Location Always flow. This PR keeps the scope narrower: Location permission copy, native i18n inventory, Info.plist background location declaration, background/significant-change monitoring gates, and focused tests.

## User Impact

Users get clearer feedback when Location Always is selected but iOS has not granted background-capable permission. Operators and reviewers also get a cleaner contract for when the iOS app may use background location behavior.

Use cases covered:

- Keep OpenClaw reachable for location-triggered/background wake-up workflows when the user explicitly selects Always and iOS grants Always.
- Show a warning when Always is selected but iOS only grants While Using, so users understand background location will not work.
- Preserve the selected Always mode in that mismatch state instead of reverting to the previous app setting.
- Show a warning when location is denied, restricted, or globally disabled in iOS settings.
- Preserve OpenClaw Location Off as an app-level gate even when iOS still allows Always or While Using.
- Show when OpenClaw is Off but iOS still allows location, without treating the OS grant as consent to re-enable OpenClaw location.
- Stop background/significant-change monitoring when the user turns Location off or downgrades away from Always.
- Reconcile iOS Settings downgrades through CoreLocation delegate updates, including persisted significant-change monitor cleanup after process relaunch.

## Evidence

- Current head: `27bbbcd63a26f98e680ace56e1b924ce05e98779`.
- Current-head consent sync proof for preserving Off/While Using under broader iOS grants: https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-99247-location-always/proof/pr-99247/current-head-consent-sync-proof.md
- Final physical iPhone proof summary and contact sheet: https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-99247-location-always/proof/pr-99247/final-physical-video-summary.md
- Redacted terminal proof artifact with rank-up coverage mapping: https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-99247-location-always/proof/pr-99247/README.md
- iPhone life-test runbook for physical proof: https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-99247-location-always/proof/pr-99247/life-test-runbook.md
- Physical iPhone video observed: iOS Always grant, OpenClaw Always summary, OpenClaw While Using under broader iOS grant, iOS downgrade to While Using, OpenClaw Always + iOS While Using mismatch warning, spinner clearing, and usable picker through the mutations.
- After that video, head `27bbbcd63a26` fixes the remaining consent-model issues: external iOS Always/While Using grants no longer promote OpenClaw Location Off back to an enabled mode, and iOS Always no longer promotes explicit OpenClaw While Using to Always.
- `pnpm native:i18n:check` passed (`entries=2453 changed=false`).
- SwiftFormat lint passed for `LocationPermissionSummary.swift` and `LocationPermissionSummaryTests.swift`.
- SwiftLint strict passed for `LocationPermissionSummary.swift` and `LocationPermissionSummaryTests.swift`.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused simulator tests passed: `OpenClawTests/LocationPermissionSummaryTests` on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5, 17 tests, covering Always/While Using mismatch, denied/global-disabled state, sticky Off under positive iOS grants, sticky While Using under iOS Always, downgrade cleanup, and significant-location monitoring eligibility.
- Built simulator app Info.plist includes `UIBackgroundModes = [audio, location, remote-notification]`.
- Prior proof build was installed on Polly's iPhone for physical recording using bundle `ai.openclawfoundation.app.test.pollybot-5y97h9j837`; local proof signing stripped personal-team entitlements, so the proof is scoped to the Location settings flow, not push/App Groups/share/widget/watch behavior.
- Local Codex review after the earlier ClawSweeper fix found no actionable regressions in the location permission summary, background monitoring controls, or Settings UI changes.

AI-assisted: yes, Codex.
